hints.title: Adjacent Parent Sum Invariant
hints.text: Each number in the triangle equals the sum of the two numbers directly above it. How can each row be constructed from its immediate predecessor?

hints.title: Boundary One and Inner Sum Invariant
hints.text: The first and last values of every row are 1, while inner entry j equals previous row j minus 1 plus previous row j.

hints.title: Row-by-Row Triangle Construction Procedure
hints.text: Initialize triangle list. For each row from 0 to numRows - 1, allocate a row of size row + 1 with boundaries set to 1. For each inner column j from 1 to row - 1, compute entry as triangle[row - 1][j - 1] + triangle[row - 1][j]. Append row to triangle and return.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N^2) time and O(N^2) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Calculating individual combinatorial combinations nCr with factorials leads to large integer calculations and redundant work.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Row-by-row dynamic accumulation computes all N * (N + 1) / 2 numbers in O(N^2) time with O(N^2) output memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should initialize row boundaries to 1 and sum adjacent pairs from the previous row.
